‘Learning and Achieving Together’
Welcome
There is something truly special about being part of a small school community...
At Graveney Primary School, our four mixed-age classes and close-knit environment allow every child to be known, supported and celebrated as they grow in confidence and develop a love of learning.
With just over 100 pupils, we are able to build strong relationships with every child and their family. Our staff know each child as an individual, recognising their strengths, interests and aspirations, which enables us to provide a personalised learning experience where every child can flourish.
Our mixed-age classes offer many unique benefits. Children learn from one another, develop confidence and build friendships across year groups. Older pupils naturally become positive role models, taking pride in supporting and encouraging younger children. This creates a caring and inclusive atmosphere where everyone feels they belong and every child has the opportunity to learn from others.
One of the first things visitors notice about Graveney is the warmth of our school community. Our children are kind, respectful and compassionate, and they genuinely care for one another. We are incredibly proud of the positive relationships that exist between pupils, staff and families, creating an environment where children feel safe, valued and happy every day.
We know that children achieve their very best when they feel secure, supported and inspired. That is why wellbeing sits at the heart of everything we do. Our dedicated staff nurture each child's confidence, encourage them to embrace new challenges and celebrate every success, helping them to become resilient, curious and enthusiastic learners.
At Graveney Primary School, we combine the warmth and personal touch of a small school with high aspirations and a broad range of opportunities, ensuring every child is equipped with the knowledge, skills and confidence to thrive both now and in the future.

pageCache.text:
After School Clubs
Our Extended School Services
Please use our Breakfast and Activity club -All bookings can be made on the school app.
Breakfast club is available from 7.30 am every day. Our Activity club is available until either 4.15pm or 5.15pm (please book the length of session you require on our app).
7:30 am - 8:30 am - £6
7:45 am - 8:30 am - £4.50
All bookable ad hoc (breakfast club by 2 pm the day before and after school club by 2 pm on the day).
After-school clubs
These are all available for bookings on the school app or directly with the provider.
For some clubs, we have limited numbers. If you would like to go on the waiting list, please speak with the school office, who will be happy to help you.
After School Clubs

pageCache.pageTitle: Graveney Primary School - School Opening Hours
pageCache.text:
School Opening Hours
When does the school day start?
Here at Graveney our school day begins at 8.30am. A member of the senior leadership team will be in the playground to welcome the children into school from 8.30am. Registration closed at 8.45am (all pupils should be in school by this time).
All our pupils are also welcome to join us for breakfast club; this opens at 7.30am and should be booked using our SchoolComms app.
From September 2023, we increased our school day to ensure that the school meets the 32.5 hours of compulsory school per week.
When do the children finish the day?
All our children are dismissed from the playground at 3.15pm. Between 3.15pm and 4.15pm we offer a range of different clubs, some of which are free for children to attend. We also offer our After-School Activity Club, which can be booked until 4.15pm or 5.15pm.
All clubs should be booked using our SchoolComms app.

Trustees and Members
Meet the Trustees and Members
Graveney Primary School became an Academy in February 2012. We are a Single Academy within a Multi Academy Trust (MAT). Our governing body consists of the Headteacher, 3 x Co-opted Trustees, 3 x Parent Trustees and 1 x Staff Trustee.
Date of Appointment Terms of Office
Headteacher, Accounting Officer
Mr Martin Wicks (Chair)
Mrs Jevgenija Tkacenko
Trustees who have resigned in the last 12 months:
Alison Blackwell resigned as Accounting Officer 07/10/2025
Rina Kreitman resigned as Member 23/09/2025
Leon Robichaud resigned on 02/06/2026
Members & the Board of Trustees of Graveney Primary School
I was born and brought up in Graveney and my children attended Graveney School. I became a Local Authority Governor in 1980 after playing a leading role in opposing a County Council proposal to close the school, as it had less than 20 pupils on role. I am a member of Swale Borough Council and KCC. I no longer sit on the Board as a Governor but remain a Member.
I have lived in Faversham for well over 30 years and began my teaching career in a girls’ secondary school in Sittingbourne. Following the births of my children, I retrained as a primary teacher and went on to serve as Headteacher in two different Kent Schools. I retired from my post at the end of December 2016. I have been chair of governors at Graveney School. I now look forward to my new role as a member of this board.
I have been associated with Graveney since 1986 when my children began school. They have now grown up and moved on, and I am still here. I am currently the staff governor; I have completed my AAT Technician and my diploma in school business management. I have been a governor here for a number of years in various different roles.
I moved to Faversham 15 years ago and have two children in a local primary school. As a Chartered Accountant with a background in both Internal and External Audit in the public and private sectors, I bring strong financial scrutiny to the Board of Governors along with a real passion to ensure children get the very best from their primary school education.
While I have only very recently moved to Whitstable, accepting a role as Trustee at Graveney is both a privilege and an opportunity to support my local community. I am a lawyer in the Government Legal Department, and so I have a particular interest in supporting the governance and compliance functions of the Graveney board.
I've lived in Kent, more specifically Sittingbourne and Canterbury, since birth. I'm currently a University Student at Canterbury. I work part-time as a Door Supervisor for venues, clubs, and bars across Kent. As well as being involved in the British Army locally. I hope to bring my experience in risk assessments and security to the school, as I value the well-being and education of both the children and guardians of schools, and hope to help as much as possible.
Jevgenija Tkacenko
I moved to Whitstable in 2018 and have one child in a local primary school. I have been working at QE in Faversham for the last five years, gaining valuable experience in education and student development. As a local tennis player and aspiring Educational Psychologist, I have a particular interest in wellbeing, learning, and personal growth. I look forward to using my experience and enthusiasm to support Graveney, its children, and the wider community as a Trustee.
Nicky Brown
I’ve always believed that every child deserves a great education and I’m passionate about making that happen. I’m a primary Headteacher and have been involved in school governance for over 20 years, in several different schools so I have a lot of knowledge and experience of teaching and learning, school finance and safeguarding. I’m really looking forward to being part of the team at Graveney Primary, working together to provide the very best primary school experience for all our children.
Michael Burr
I live in Graveney and my children attend Graveney Primary School. I have a finance background, having worked in the FMCG sector, where I developed strong experience in financial planning, analysis, and strategic decision-making. I am passionate about the school and the role it plays in the local community, and I am keen to use my skills and experience to support its continued success and ensure the best possible outcomes for all pupils.
Evie Crickson
I have always believed that every child deserves the opportunity to thrive and achieve their very best. I have been teaching for eleven years across all primary year groups and am currently the SENCO at Graveney Primary. These roles have given me valuable experience in teaching, learning, inclusion, and supporting children with a wide range of needs. I am passionate about making our school an inclusive, happy place where every child feels safe, valued, and ready to learn. As a Staff Governor, I am committed to helping Graveney continue to be a community that feels like a family, where children are supported to grow in confidence, develop a love of learning, and reach their full potential.

Remote Learning
Remote Learning will be provided for pupils who are unable to attend school in person when appropriate.
This will only take place using Microsoft Teams. All our learners will be provided with access to their class team.
Teachers will all be providing daily lessons for pupils to complete. Each day there will be a Literacy, Maths and at least one other subject for your child to complete. Staff will be checking daily that pupils are accessing the learning provided. As a school, we will endeavour to continue to provide the full, broad and balanced curriculum for all our learners.
All learning should be accessed through Microsoft Teams. Staff will set assignments for the pupils each day. Posts can also be used to chat with friends in class or ask for help. Posts will be monitored by staff throughout the day. However, please remember that staff may also be teaching pupils in school and will not always be able to respond immediately.
Staff will be able to give feedback on all work submitted, giving feedback and completing assessments our pupils learning.
Teams is available on various devices. If you require support with devices to enable your child to be able to access their learning, please contact the school. We do have some which can be loaned for you to use at home – you will be expected to sign our user agreement and contract for all devices borrowed.
If, for any reason, your child has difficulty engaging in remote learning, please let me know as soon as possible to discuss how the school can support the learning in these circumstances.
Staff will be checking that ALL pupils are accessing the remote learning daily. Pupils are expected to have access to the following amounts of remote learning.
As a school, we have high expectations. However, please remember that not all pupils will be able to complete all the learning set by the teacher every day. We ask that all pupils attempt each task set and try their hardest to complete as much as possible in the time available. Remember that the time is not all teacher-led - it also includes their other learning, including discussions and all the fun tasks they can help with at home. Pupils should also be accessing their independent learning on My Maths and TT Rockstars.
Lessons will use a variety of resources. Some of these may be clips from your teacher (short videos), some will be from Oaks National Academy or YouTube. We will try to limit the need to print documents at home for learning as not all families have access to a printer.
As a school, we have decided not to broadcast live lessons. Doing this would place many of our families at a disadvantage as they are sharing devices and many parents also work at home, making it very difficult for them to access them at set times daily. Teachers will be available to answer your questions throughout the day using posts in your class team.
Our Acceptable Use of Technology Policy is available in the Policy section of this website.
Alison Blackwell - Headteacher

PE and School Sport
Sports Premium Grant
All children and young people should live healthy active lives. The UK Chief Medical Officers recommend that all children and young people should take part in moderate to vigorous intensity physical activity for at least 60 minutes every day. Children with special educational needs and disabilities should take part in 20 minutes of daily activity.
The Childhood Obesity Plan says that at least 30 minutes of daily activity should take place in schools.
Schools have a key role to play in achieving this aim. This is particularly true of primary schools where the foundations of positive and enjoyable participation in regular physical activity are embedded. All children should have equal access to high-quality PE provision and opportunities to experience and participate in a wide range of sports and physical activities. Academic achievement can improve in school because of the benefits children can gain.
Schools should use the PE and sport premium funding to help achieve these aims. It must not be used for core-type school activities. They should use it to make additional and sustainable improvements to the PE, sport and physical activity they provide, such as:
Schools should prioritise PE and sport premium spending to improve in the following 5 key areas:
increase participation in competitive sport
